title: A Standardized Culture Medium for Comparative Drug Efficacy Evaluation Across Plasmodium and Babesia Species
author: Pratap Vydyam
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML

steps.title: Prepare human packed RBCs
steps.instruction: Centrifuge A+ packed RBCs at 1,000 rcf (acceleration 9, brake 0) for 15 min at 4 °C. Wash the pellet three times with 10 mL cold 1× PBS, centrifuging each wash at 700 rcf for 5 min. Resuspend the washed cells in incomplete RPMI‑1640 to a 50 % hematocrit (e.g., 10 mL packed RBCs + 10 mL DFS20) and store at 4 °C.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at 1,000 rcf, 15 min, 4 °C.
Wash three times with 10 mL cold 1× PBS, 700 rcf, 5 min each.
Resuspend to 50 % hematocrit in incomplete RPMI‑1640 and store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Determine parasitemia and adjust culture
steps.instruction: Make thin blood smears from stock Babesia and Plasmodium cultures, fix 10 s, stain with Giemsa Solution I for 30 s then Solution II for 30 s, wash, air‑dry. Count ≥3,000 RBCs under 100× oil immersion across 10 fields to calculate parasitemia. Dilute the cultures with fresh RBCs in complete DFS20 and/or RPMI‑1640 to obtain 0.2 % parasitemia at 5 % hematocrit for the assay. Calculate the in‑vitro parasitemia count as described in references [33,35,42].

substeps.instruction: Prepare and stain thin smears (fix 10 s, Giemsa I 30 s, Giemsa II 30 s).
Count ≥3,000 RBCs at 100× oil immersion across 10 fields.
Dilute cultures to 0.2 % parasitemia, 5 % hematocrit in complete medium.

steps.title: Maintain and synchronize stock cultures
steps.instruction: Store fresh human RBCs at 50 % hematocrit at 4 °C for up to two weeks. Keep routine asexual cultures at 2–5 % hematocrit and 1–3 % parasitemia; dilute if >5 % parasitemia. Culture Babesia duncani (WA‑1), B. divergens (Rouen87) and B. MO1 in DFS20 at 5 % hematocrit, 37 °C, gas 2 % O₂, 5 % CO₂, 93 % N₂; change medium daily and monitor by Giemsa‑stained smears. Culture P. falciparum (3D7, Dd2, HB3) in RPMI‑1640 complete medium at 3–5 % hematocrit, 37 °C, gas 4 % O₂, 5 % CO₂, 91 % N₂; change medium daily. Subculture every two generations, keep parasitemia 1–4 %, and synchronize Plasmodium cultures every 5–8 generations. Include all three antibiotics (penicillin/streptomycin, gentamicin, etc.) when culturing multiple species; gentamicin alone is sufficient for most cultures.

substeps.instruction: Store fresh RBCs at 50 % HCT, 4 °C ≤2 weeks.
Maintain routine cultures at 2–5 % HCT, 1–3 % parasitemia; dilute >5 %.
Babesia: DFS20, 5 % HCT, 37 °C, 2 % O₂/5 % CO₂/93 % N₂; change daily.
Plasmodium: RPMI‑1640, 3–5 % HCT, 37 °C, 4 % O₂/5 % CO₂/91 % N₂; change daily.
Subculture every two generations; synchronize Plasmodium every 5–8 generations.
Use full antibiotic cocktail for mixed‑species work; gentamicin alone is acceptable.

steps.title: Prepare drug stock solutions
steps.instruction: Dissolve each antifolate compound in 100 % DMSO to a final concentration of 10 mM. Vortex for 10–15 s to ensure complete dissolution. Store the 10 mM stocks at –20 °C. If precipitation occurs, warm to 50 °C, vortex again, or use an ultrasonic bath.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve compounds in DMSO to 10 mM.
Vortex 10–15 s.
Store at –20 °C.
Troubleshoot precipitation by warming or sonication.

steps.title: Create working drug dilutions
steps.instruction: Perform serial 2‑fold dilutions of the 10 mM stocks in complete DFS20 medium to generate either a 4‑step or 12‑step concentration series (e.g., final assay concentrations of 100, 50, 10, 5 nM down to 0.049 nM). Use a 96‑well clear flat‑bottom plate for the dilutions to allow multichannel pipetting. Keep the final DMSO concentration in assay wells ≤0.5 % (v/v). Prepare the dilutions at 2× the intended assay concentration and make fresh on the day of the experiment.

substeps.instruction: Serially dilute 2‑fold in DFS20 to obtain desired range.
Use 96‑well clear plate for ease of multichannel pipetting.
Maintain DMSO ≤0.5 % in final wells.
Prepare 2× working solutions fresh on experiment day.

steps.title: Set up 96‑well assay plate
steps.instruction: In a 96‑well flat‑clear bottom plate, add 100 µL DFS20 medium to every well except the first column of each drug series. Add 200 µL of each 2× drug dilution to the first column triplicate wells (e.g., rows A–F). Perform a 2‑fold serial dilution by transferring 100 µL from the first well to the next across the row, discarding the final 100 µL from the 12th well to keep volumes consistent. Add 100 µL DFS20 containing 0.5 % DMSO to no‑drug control wells (H1–H3). Add 100 µL DFS20 with 2 µM WR99210 (for Babesia) or 10× IC₅₀ chloroquine (for Plasmodium) to positive‑control wells (H4–H6). Gently pipette to ensure a uniform cell suspension before dispensing.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 µL DFS20 to all wells except first drug column.
Add 200 µL 2× drug solutions to first column triplicates.
Serially dilute 2‑fold across the row, discard 100 µL from last well.
Add 100 µL DFS20 + 0.5 % DMSO to negative controls (H1–H3).
Add 100 µL DFS20 + 2 µM WR99210 or 10× IC₅₀ CQ to positive controls (H4–H6).
Pipette gently to keep suspension uniform.

steps.title: Add parasite cultures to assay
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of parasite culture (0.4 % parasitemia, 10 % hematocrit, 2× concentration) to each test well containing the 2× drug dilutions, bringing the final volume to 200 µL (1× drug, 1× parasite). Add 100 µL of uninfected RBCs (10 % hematocrit in DFS20) to background control wells (H10–H12). For Plasmodium cultures originally grown in RPMI‑1640, wash twice with DFS20 (700 rcf, 5 min, room temperature) before adding. Use a multichannel pipette and dispense slowly to avoid bubbles.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 µL 0.4 % parasitemia, 10 % HCT, 2× culture to test wells.
Add 100 µL uninfected RBCs (10 % HCT) to background controls.
Wash RPMI‑grown Plasmodium cultures twice with DFS20 (700 rcf, 5 min, RT).
Use multichannel pipette, dispense slowly.

steps.title: Incubate plates for drug exposure
steps.instruction: Cover the plate with a low‑evaporation lid and incubate at 37 °C in a humidified chamber flushed with 4 % O₂, 5 % CO₂, and 91 % N₂ for 72 h.

substeps.instruction: Cover with low‑evaporation lid.
Incubate 37 °C, 4 % O₂/5 % CO₂/91 % N₂, humidified, 72 h.

steps.title: Prepare SYBR Green‑I lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Make lysis buffer in distilled water containing 0.008 % saponin, 0.08 % Triton X‑100, 20 mM Tris‑HCl (pH 7.5), 5 mM EDTA, and 0.01 % SYBR Green‑I. Protect the buffer from light and store at –20 °C.

substeps.instruction: Combine reagents to final concentrations listed.
Protect from light; store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Lyse cultures and transfer to black plate
steps.instruction: After the 72‑h incubation, remove the clear‑bottom plate, gently resuspend each well by pipetting up and down five times. Transfer 100 µL of each resuspended culture to a new black flat‑bottom 96‑well plate that already contains 100 µL SYBR Green‑I lysis buffer. Mix gently.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend wells by pipetting up/down 5×.
Transfer 100 µL culture to black plate with 100 µL lysis buffer.
Mix gently.

steps.title: Incubate for DNA staining
steps.instruction: Incubate the black‑plate at 37 °C in the dark (cover with aluminum foil) for 15 min to allow complete lysis and DNA staining (longer up to 1 h if required).

substeps.instruction: Incubate 37 °C, dark, 15 min (up to 1 h if needed).

steps.title: Measure fluorescence
steps.instruction: Read fluorescence on a BioTek Synergy Mx (or equivalent, e.g., Spectra Mx) using excitation at 480 nm and emission at 540 nm (540 nm accepted; 520 nm also reported). Keep plates protected from light during reading.

substeps.instruction: Set reader to 480 nm excitation, 540 nm emission.
Measure fluorescence; protect from light.

steps.title: Analyze data and calculate IC50
steps.instruction: Export raw fluorescence values to Excel. Compute the average fluorescence of the uninfected RBC (background) wells and subtract this value from all test, negative‑control (0.1 % DMSO), and positive‑control wells. Calculate % growth = [(F_test – F_pos)/(F_neg – F_pos)] × 100 and % inhibition = 100 – % growth. Plot % inhibition versus log₁₀ drug concentration in GraphPad Prism, fit a variable‑slope sigmoidal dose‑response curve, and obtain IC₅₀ values with standard deviations from three independent experiments (each with technical triplicates). Negative control (0.1 % DMSO) defines 0 % inhibition; positive control (WR99210 or chloroquine) defines 100 % inhibition. Remove obvious outliers if curves appear irregular.

substeps.instruction: Export fluorescence to Excel.
Subtract background (uninfected RBC) from all wells.
Calculate % growth and % inhibition.
Plot % inhibition vs log drug concentration in GraphPad Prism.
Fit variable‑slope sigmoidal curve to obtain IC₅₀ ± SD.
Use three independent experiments with technical triplicates.
Treat 0.1 % DMSO as 0 % inhibition, WR99210/CQ as 100 % inhibition.
Remove outliers if needed.

description: Validation of protocol This protocol (or parts of it) has been used and validated in the following research article: Vydyam et al. [33]. In vitro efficacy of next-generation dihydrotriazines and biguanides against babesiosis and malaria parasites. Antimicrob Agents Chemother (Figure 4).
